- Preserve plain fallback model display and non-Codex behavior.

## Tests
- `npm run build`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/model-display.test.js`

Closes #399

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #400 closes [issue #399](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/399), which investigated inconsistent answer-route footer metadata between fresh and resumed Codex runs.
- The approved direction was to keep both answer paths on the same template while normalizing Codex GPT-5 encoded reasoning into a stable footer shape.
- This PR extracts footer/session model display logic into `model-display.ts`, adds focused tests, and updates `run.ts` to call the helper.
- The core GPT-5 normalization works in isolation, but the current head still breaks an existing test and has one display/runtime semantics mismatch for suffixed Codex model IDs.

## Review
- Overall, the implementation is small and aligned with the main issue plan, but it is not ready to ship because a current test failure is verified at PR head.
- Reviewer outputs agree on the stale `envelope.test.ts` failure; there is a meaningful disagreement on whether non-GPT-5 Codex suffix behavior is in scope, so that is treated as a warning rather than a second blocker.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Stale envelope source guard breaks test suite | BLOCKING | The PR imports the new helper from `model-display.ts`, but `envelope.test.ts` still asserts the moved symbols exist in `run.ts`; verified `node --test dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js` fails 1/74 after build. |
| Codex suffixed-model display diverges from adapter semantics | WARNING | `model-display.ts` only decomposes GPT-5 suffixes, while `resolveAcpxModelSelection` treats any suffixed Codex model as encoded and drops separate `thoughtLevel`, so non-GPT-5 suffixed Codex footers can show a reasoning value runtime ignored. |
| Optional helper coverage gaps | INFO | New tests cover the requested footer cases, but they do not directly verify a valid session log model line, default-model rendering, or encoded model with empty env reasoning. |

## Progress
- Rubrics review passed and confirmed the diff is surgical.
- Verified at PR head: `npm --prefix .agent run build` passed and `node --test dist/__tests__/model-display.test.js` passed.
- Verified at PR head: `node --test dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js` failed on the stale source assertion.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis; posted inline comments on [`run.ts:63`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/400#discussion_r3345301553) and [`model-display.ts:47`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/400#discussion_r3345302323).
- No comments were minimized, no replies were added, and no threads were resolved.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Stale envelope source guard breaks test suite</summary>

**Cause:** [`envelope.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/34f677ffc8204fd8fe52c48ecccf52ec0696cda0/.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts#L1168-L1169) still checks `run.ts` for `CODEX_REASONING_MODEL_SUFFIX` and `displayReasoningEffort`, but this PR moved/replaced that display logic via [`run.ts:63`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/34f677ffc8204fd8fe52c48ecccf52ec0696cda0/.agent/src/run.ts#L63).

**Candidate solutions:** Update the guard to inspect the new helper contract in `model-display.ts`, or remove the brittle source-name assertions now that behavior is covered by focused tests. Rebuild and rerun the envelope test.

**Comments:** Both code reviewers flagged this, and local verification reproduced the failure.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Codex suffixed-model display diverges from adapter semantics</summary>

**Cause:** [`model-display.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/34f677ffc8204fd8fe52c48ecccf52ec0696cda0/.agent/src/model-display.ts#L47-L52) only decomposes suffixed GPT-5 Codex models, but [`resolveAcpxModelSelection`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/34f677ffc8204fd8fe52c48ecccf52ec0696cda0/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L246-L256) treats any suffixed Codex model as encoded and suppresses separate thought level.

**Candidate solutions:** Share the suffix parsing semantics with the adapter, or preserve legacy suppression for non-GPT-5 suffixed Codex models instead of rendering the env reasoning effort separately. Update the current non-GPT-5 Codex test expectation if behavior changes.

**Comments:** Claude/rubrics treated GPT-5 scope as acceptable; Codex flagged this as adapter drift. Because the old display path suppressed separate reasoning for any suffixed Codex model, the synthesis keeps this as a real warning.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Optional helper coverage gaps</summary>

**Cause:** The new tests focus on footer normalization paths, but `extractSessionModel` is only exercised through a fallback case.

**Candidate solutions:** Add direct tests for a valid `session` log model, empty model rendering as `default model`, and an encoded model with empty env reasoning.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The stale suite guard is a verified branch failure, and the Codex suffix display mismatch is a small code/test alignment fix suitable for automated follow-up.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

- [ ] Align Codex suffixed-model footer normalization with `resolveAcpxModelSelection` or legacy suppression, and update the non-GPT-5 Codex test expectation accordingly.

Is the gpt5 prefix etc overly hacky? Is it a generic enough implementation

I would not call it overly hacky for this PR. It is provider-specific, but it is scoped to the provider behavior that already exists in ACPX model selection: Codex GPT-5 reasoning is encoded into model IDs like `gpt-5.5/xhigh`, while other providers keep reasoning separate.

The `gpt-5` prefix check is reasonable as a guard, not a generic abstraction. It prevents the display formatter from splitting arbitrary slash-looking model names while still handling the known Codex GPT-5 shape: [`model-display.ts#L1-L27`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1ca755094549b68a565fd98fa82e6cc27d93d230/.agent/src/model-display.ts#L1-L27). That lines up with the runtime adapter’s existing semantics: [`acpx-adapter.ts#L232-L275`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1ca755094549b68a565fd98fa82e6cc27d93d230/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L232-L275).

So my read is:

- Generic enough at the display boundary: `buildModelDisplay` still takes `agent`, `model`, `reasoningEffort`, and `runnerName`, then normalizes only when needed: [`model-display.ts#L44-L78`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1ca755094549b68a565fd98fa82e6cc27d93d230/.agent/src/model-display.ts#L44-L78).
- Intentionally not provider-generic inside the Codex branch. That is fine because this is not a universal model parser; it is formatting ACPX/Codex effective model metadata.
- The one real maintainability caveat is duplicated Codex suffix knowledge between `acpx-adapter.ts` and `model-display.ts`. I would not block on that now, but if this grows, the right follow-up is to extract a shared `codex-model` helper for parse/compose semantics.

The tests cover the important anti-hacky cases: GPT-5 slash/bracket split, resumed fallback, non-GPT-5 Codex suffix suppression, and non-Codex passthrough: [`model-display.test.ts#L6-L59`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1ca755094549b68a565fd98fa82e6cc27d93d230/.agent/src/__tests__/model-display.test.ts#L6-L59). So I’d treat this as acceptable and surgical, with a small future refactor only if Codex model encoding keeps expanding.
